Karthik / Priyom / Tessa — reviewing Helix's questionnaire. Summary answers below (I prepared a document with line-by-line responses; see attached 'Redwood_Legal_Q_Responses_20260303.docx' and a proposed order form PDF). I kept positions commercially reasonable to enable progression while protecting Redwood's IP and limiting open-ended exposure.

Executive summary (short bullets for procurement):
- IP / Model outputs: Redwood does not claim ownership of customer-provided data or customer-provided prompts. For model outputs, we grant customers a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license to use outputs for their business purposes. We decline assignment of underlying model IP or training weights.
- Indemnity: Redwood will provide IP infringement indemnity limited to use of the service as provided and in accordance with documentation; will not indemnify for third-party prompts that induce infringing outputs beyond our control.
- Liability cap: Standard commercial cap — aggregate liability limited to the greater of (i) fees paid by Helix to Redwood under the Order Form in the 12 months prior to the claim or (ii) $5,000,000. We are open to limited carve-outs for gross negligence or willful misconduct (not indemnified by cap).
- Order form / Data: Proposed order form clarifies data handling (customer data segregation, optional KV caching controls, retention windows configurable), SOC2 Type II evidence available via NDA, and KMS support for private deployments.

Specific responses (high level excerpts):
1) IP ownership Q1 (Do you assign IP to buyer?) — No. We grant a license to outputs. Rationale: models and weights are Redwood proprietary; customers need rights to outputs to operate.
2) IP infringement indemnity Q4 — We accept a limited IP infringement indemnity for claims arising from the service when used as intended. Exclusions: claims arising from customer's prompts or combination with third-party data.
3) Liability cap Q9 — See above; offers a balanced commercial cap tied to spend or $5M floor. For enterprise or large committed deals we can discuss alternative caps tied to multi-year committed spend.
4) Order form changes — redline attached. Key redlines: (a) explicit SLA and remedy table for Dedicated capacity, (b) termination-for-convenience language retained but with 60-day notice for enterprise SOWs, (c) data deletion certification upon contract expiration in Private deployments.

Attachments: Redwood_Legal_Q_Responses_20260303.docx (contains responses to each numbered question), Redwood_Proposed_Order_Form_20260303.pdf (clean and redline available on request).

If Helix needs a higher liability cap we should evaluate on a case-by-case basis tied to committed revenue; I recommend we keep the standard cap for initial contract.

Laura Bennett
Lead Counsel, Commercial Transactions
Redwood Inference

Sara — thanks for the questionnaire and for the time last week. Apologies for the brief delay; we wanted final sign-off from legal on a couple of positions. Please find our consolidated responses below and attached.

What we are returning:
- Redwood_Legal_Q_Responses_20260303.docx (line-by-line answers to the questionnaire)
- Redwood_Proposed_Order_Form_20260303.pdf (clean copy)
- DocuSign order form link: https://www.docusign.net/HELIX-RWD-OF-2026 (we can prepare a redline in DocuSign if you prefer)

High-level positions (for your procurement/legal):
- IP / Outputs: Redwood does not take ownership of customer data or customer-provided prompts. For model outputs, Redwood grants Helix a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license to use outputs for Helix's internal business purposes and to sublicense to its affiliates and service providers. We will not assign underlying model weights or proprietary model code.
- Indemnity: Redwood will indemnify for third-party IP claims to the extent such claims arise from Redwood's services used as intended and without unauthorized modifications. We will not accept indemnity for claims resulting from customer-supplied prompts or combination with third-party models.
- Liability cap: Our standard cap is the greater of (a) fees paid by Helix to Redwood under the applicable Order Form in the 12 months preceding the claim, or (b) $5,000,000. Exceptions for gross negligence/willful misconduct and for rights to injunctive relief are carved out. For larger committed agreements we can discuss an alternative cap tied to committed multi-year spend.
- Data / Compliance: SOC2 Type II report and PCI/other evidence available upon execution of an NDA; Private deployments can be configured with customer-managed KMS and strict retention controls (we detail options in the attached order form).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Please review the attached docx and proposed order form and tell us which items Helix needs us to escalate.
2) If the liability cap is a blocker, let us know the alternate structure Helix prefers and we will put it on the table for commercial consideration.
3) If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-min call with Laura (lead counsel) and Priyom (solutions lead) to walk the legal team through the redlines.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.
